data.title: Tesla's Self-Driving Is an American Marvel — Barrons.com
data.description:
To the Editor: Great article ("Can General Motors and Ford Survive the Flood of Cheap Chinese EVs?" Cover Story, Oct. 30). But there's no mention of Tesla's full self-driving capability, a technological marvel and revolution available today. How long will Tesla hold that competitive advantage?

Vik Kasparian On Barrons.com

Disorganized Dems?

To the Editor: Andy Serwer quoted a political analyst as saying that Democrats aren't smart enough to nominate Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear in 2028 ("If the Democrats Want to Scare the GOP, This Presidential Candidate Could Be Just the Ticket," Up & Down Wall Street, Oct. 29). I'm reminded of Will Rogers' famous joke: "I belong to no organized political party. I'm a Democrat."

Don Wittenberger Shoreline, Wash.

Crypto ETFs

To the Editor: Lewis Braham points out that many new cryptocurrency exchange-traded funds generate income for shareholders by selling put and call options ("The Rise of the New Actively Managed Crypto ETFs," Funds, Oct. 28). Owning Bitcoin is almost always more risky than betting on sports or participating in a zero-sum crap game.

If there is ever again a terrible day like Black Monday, Oct. 19, 1987, I'd rather be in stocks like NextEra Energy and Union Pacific, which sport revenue, earnings, and dividends, all of which cryptocurrencies lack.

Anthony Bavedas Shelton, Conn.

Buy, Borrow, Die

To the Editor: "Big Homes, Big Loans" (Review & Preview, Oct. 30) notes that the stock market is delivering returns higher than mortgage rates. But it doesn't relate the increase in superjumbo mortgages to the increase in the use of tax-avoidance strategies by the very wealthy. They use the loans to avoid triggering massive capital-gains tax liabilities while maintaining investment momentum — the "buy, borrow, die" playbook.

Craig Chaffee Sacramento, Calif.

The Invisible Hand

To the Editor: I will continue to favor companies committed to Milton Friedman's business philosophy of reacting to Adam Smith's "invisible hand" ("The Investor's Case for Protecting Democracy," Other Voices, Oct. 29). The authors' utopian argument — that "from a purely self-interested point of view, businesspeople should care about civic dysfunction if they want to protect their profits" — has been tried many times and results in political grift, attacks on liberty, and lower standards of living.

Richard Saler On Barrons.com

data.title: Fitch Raises Cyprus Rating on Declining Debt
data.description:
By Stephen Nakrosis

Fitch Ratings said it raised Cyprus' long-term issuer default ratings to A from A-, and assigned a stable outlook.

The nation's rapidly declining debt was one factor cited by Fitch in its upgrade. Cyprus is expected to have a general government surplus of 3.2% of GDP in 2026, highest in the euro zone, Fitch said. The country's general government debt is seen falling to 46.3% of GDP in 2026 from 52.4% in 2025, with expectations it will drop further, to 36.6%, in 2028.

Fitch also forecasts GDP growth of 3% in 2026 to 2028, above the euro zone average, driven by strong domestic consumption and continued positive performance in services sectors.

Fitch said Cyrpus' tourism inflows have recovered quickly after a slowdown at onset of Middle East conflict.

However, the nation faces inflation challenges, reflecting its high reliance on fossil fuel imports and elevated service prices. Fitch said harmonized inflation in the country was 5.2% in September, up from 0.9% in February. Inflation is expected to average 2.5% next year and in 2027 and 2028, from 4% this year.

The nation's current account deficit is expected to average 8.1% of GDP in 2026 to 2028, Fitch said.

Short-term risks center on inflation pressures and its effect on consumption, while external vulnerabilities are a key medium-term challenge, Fitch added.

Write to Stephen Nakrosis at stephen.nakrosis@wsj.com

data.title: Nuclear Reactor Firm Oklo Beats Earnings Expectations. That's Not Why the Stock Is Up. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Anita Hamilton

Shares of nuclear reactor start-up Oklo, formerly chaired by OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, closed sharply higher Friday following its third quarter earnings report.

But because the company doesn't have a commercial product yet — its flagship commercial nuclear reactor called Aurora won't be up and running until 2028 at the earliest — its revenue and earnings figures aren't what excited investors.

Instead, the steps Oklo revealed on progress toward developing its small nuclear reactors measuring just 5,000 square feet in size were what impressed.

Most tangibly, it showed that its planned powerhouse at the Department of Energy's Idaho National Laboratory had advanced to the stage where structural steel is now in place. This is a demonstration project aimed at proving its technology works.

It also announced a new deal with U.S. Forged Rings for critical components needed for up to 27 Aurora modules through 2035.

And it affirmed that the plant it is developing in Ohio to supply 1.2 gigawatts of power for Meta data centers is still expected to start generating power in 2030.

Investors also were assured by the company's more than $3 billion in cash and marketable securities. That means the company has plenty of runway to keep up development.

"We see continued progress across several of the key building blocks needed to support future deployment, though significant execution remains ahead," Truist analysts wrote after the report.

Texas Capital's Nate Pendleton added that "Oklo is building a differentiated platform that can deliver on the promise of advanced nuclear power."

Oklo's top-line earnings numbers for the three months ending in September were revenue of $1.9 million, above analysts' estimates of $1 million. It reported no revenue during the same period last year. Losses were 22 cents a share versus the 27 cents analysts were expecting.

Its adjusted net losses widened from a year ago to $47.6 million, up from $29.7 million during the same period in 2025.

Shares closed up 23% at $23.58 on Friday. They're still down 67% for the year.

Write to Anita Hamilton at anita.hamilton@barrons.com

data.title: BP says Whiting, Indiana refinery offered to meet union, awaits response
data.description:
BP on Friday said representatives from its 440,000-barrel-per-day oil refinery in Whiting, Indiana had offered to meet United Steelworkers Local 7-1 next week but had yet to receive confirmation from the union.

"At our last negotiating session on Monday, October 26, BP again provided revised contract language to address union concerns. We had also expected the union to bring revised contract language for consideration, but it did not," the company said in a statement.

  • BP said it has repeatedly sought to establish a regular cadence of meetings so the parties can steadily work through the issues that remain, but the union has not agreed to an ongoing schedule of negotiating sessions.

  • Although BP has continued to provide information and revised contract language to address union concerns, the union has not offered any new contract language, counterproposals, or anything new for consideration since May, it said.

  • Following the October 26 meeting, BP said it proposed meeting this week on Monday, Wednesday, and Thursday, but no meetings were confirmed.

  • BP added that it is ready to meet as often as needed, whether through formal bargaining, informal discussions or federal mediation.

About MediPharm Labs Founded in 2015, MediPharm Labs specializes in the development and manufacture of purified, pharmaceutical-quality cannabis concentrates, active pharmaceutical ingredients (API) and advanced derivative products utilizing a Good Manufacturing Practices certified facility with ISO standard-built clean rooms. MediPharm Labs has invested in an expert, research-driven team, state-of-the-art technology, downstream purification methodologies and purpose-built facilities for delivery of pure, trusted and precision-dosed cannabis products for its customers. MediPharm Labs develops, formulates, processes, packages and distributes cannabis and advanced cannabinoid-based products to domestic and international medical markets.

In 2021, MediPharm Labs received a Pharmaceutical Drug Establishment License from Health Canada, becoming the only company in North America to hold a commercial-scale domestic Good Manufacturing Practices License for the extraction of multiple natural cannabinoids. This acquisition also included Harvest Medical Clinics in Canada which provides medical cannabis patients with physician consultations for medical cannabis education and prescriptions.

data.description:
• Gladstone Land Corporation is expected to show a fall in quarterly revenue when it reports results on November 10 for the period ending September 30 2026

  • The Mclean Virginia-based company is expected to report a 1.4% decrease in revenue to $17.534 million from $17.79 million a year ago, according to the mean estimate from 5 analysts, based on LSEG data.

  • ​LSEG's mean analyst estimate for Gladstone Land Corporation is for a loss of 13 cents per share.

  • The current average analyst rating on the shares is "hold" and the breakdown of recommendations is 1 "strong buy" or "buy," 4 "hold" and no "sell" or "strong sell."

  • The mean earnings estimate of analysts was unchanged in the last three months. ​

  • Wall Street's median 12-month price target for Gladstone Land Corporation is $9.75, about 38.9% above its last closing price of $7.02
